items.name: Bihing Tahik
items.summary: A beach resort about 3 km from Sanga-Sanga Airport whose buildings are shaped after the giant clam.
detail: Bihing Tahik means by the sea in the local language. Architect Deo Alrashid Alam of the firm DADA based its design on the curves of the giant clam shell, which are regarded as the jade of the sea, and the resort uses the design to draw attention to giant clam conservation.
Travel guides recommend it for the sunset.

before_you_go: Do not touch or chase the turtles.

do.title: Snorkel with the turtles
do.detail: Green sea turtles swim over the reef off the beach.

items.name: Silisad Beach
items.summary: A beach in Bongao under Bud Bongao where green sea turtles swim over the reef.
detail: A winning photo in the 2021 regional photo contest of the Ministry of Trade, Investments and Tourism was taken at Silisad: Bud Bongao Forest Park above, and a green sea turtle over coral in clear water below.
The ministry describes snorkelling or diving here with turtles swimming alongside.

before_you_go: Bring cash: guides report that no establishments in Bongao accept cards.
items.getting_there: In downtown Bongao, reached on foot or by tricycle.
items.best_time: Before noon if you are catching a boat: public boats to Simunul usually leave around midday.

do.title: Walk the market and the pier
do.detail: Guides suggest a walk around the market and the old Chinese Pier.

do.title: Catch a public boat to the islands
do.detail: Public boats run from the Chinese Pier to Simunul, Sibutu, Sitangkai, Sipangkot and Liyaburan; other islands need a hired boat.

items.name: Bongao Chinese Pier and public market
items.summary: Downtown Bongao's old pier, where boats leave for the outer islands, next to the town's public market.
detail: The Chinese Pier is the busy waterfront of downtown Bongao. Public boats leave from here for Simunul, Sibutu, Sitangkai, Sipangkot and Liyaburan, and painted motorboats tie up beside colourful lepa boats.
Guides pair it with a walk through the public market, where jeepneys leave daily for Panglima Sugala and Languyan.

eat.title: Mardo's, if you are not in a hurry
eat.detail: The busy downtown cafe on the Circumferential Road warns on its menu that patience is a virtue; Tawi-Tawi kitchens can ask for 4 hours' notice for specials such as kinilaw.

eat.title: Pastries at the port-side cafe
eat.detail: A small cafe by the port puts a plate of pastries in front of every customer, and you pay only for what you eat.

eat.title: Curacha and lobster
eat.detail: Giant curacha crabs and big lobsters are caught around Tawi-Tawi and are much more affordable here than in other fishing towns.

eat.title: Tarambulan at the Ramadhan food market
eat.detail: During Ramadhan the food market comes alive in the late afternoon; tarambulan, a folded pancake heaped with chocolate, is a favourite. The provincial Ramadhan Night Market at the Masjid Raayat complex runs 6 pm to 11 pm.

before_you_go: It is a grave and a place of prayer: dress modestly and ask before taking photos.
Let the municipality know before you arrive in Sibutu.
items.getting_there: By public boat from the Chinese Pier in Bongao to Sibutu.
items.best_time: 7 November is Sheikh Karimul Makhdum Day, marking the arrival of Islam.

do.title: See the structure in front of the grave at Tandu Banak
do.detail: An unfinished building stands in front of what is believed to be Sheik Karimul Makhdum's grave at Tandu Banak.

do.title: Take the boat to Tandu Banak
do.detail: An older account took a boat of about 3 hours from Bongao's Chinese Pier to Tandu Banak for under PHP 200; a 2026 listing gives Wita Ferries weekday trips from Bongao to Sibutu of about 1 hour. Check with the boatmen the day before.

items.name: Burial Site of Sheik Karimol Makhdum
items.summary: The grave in Tandu Banak, Sibutu, of the 14th-century missionary who brought Islam to the Philippines, declared a National Historical Shrine.
detail: Sheik Karimol Makhdum is the missionary credited with founding the first mosque in the country at Tubig Indangan, Simunul. His burial site at Tandu Banak in Sibutu is declared a National Historical Shrine.

The National Historical Commission of the Philippines installed a marker here on 6 November 2023, the day before the marker at his mosque in Simunul. Accounts differ on where he lies: a SunStar travel feature says his remains are buried beside the mosque in Simunul.

before_you_go: Mapun is far out from Bongao; arrange the trip with the provincial tourism office and the municipality.
items.best_time: Early September, for Mapun Day.

images.author: Edil Hairon
images.caption: The municipal hall of Mapun

items.name: Mapun
items.summary: A remote island far out in the Sulu Sea, home of the Jama Mapun, with freshwater lakes and rocky cliffs.
detail: Mapun lies in the Sulu Sea north-west of the rest of Tawi-Tawi. It holds freshwater lakes, among them Lake Ernestine, Lake Sapah and Lake Singuan, along with springs and rocky cliffs, and turtles are raised on the islets around it.

The Magellan-Elcano expedition passed here and described the people as Muslim and brave fighters. The National Historical Commission placed a Quincentennial marker on Isla Keana, Barangay Iruk-Iruk, in 2021.
Mapun Day, the town's foundation day, is on 5 September, after a week of contests in song, dance, oration and the Budjang Mapun pageant.

before_you_go: It is an active volcano: check the PHIVOLCS bulletin before going near it.
Arrange visits outside Marawi through the provincial tourism office and go with local companions.
items.getting_there: There is no established trail. A 2013 exploration climb with local guides, coordinated with local officials, took 20 hours of hiking to the summit and 17 to come down over 5 days, camping by a river in a valley.

do.title: See it from Mount Matampor
do.detail: The campsite on Mount Matampor in Balindong looks across Lake Lanao to Mount Ragang.

do.title: Climb into the mossy forest
do.detail: The lower trail is overgrown with rattan, but above 2,000 metres a mossy forest covers the slopes and the summit.

do.title: Look out over Lake Lanao and 3 provinces
do.detail: Where the moss forest opens, the view takes in Lake Lanao and the towns of Maguindanao, Lanao del Sur and Cotabato.

images.author: Kenneth Magbanua
images.caption: Mount Ragang in the background, over dry hill country

items.name: Mount Ragang
items.summary: An active stratovolcano of 2,815 metres, the highest point of Lanao del Sur and the seventh highest mountain in the country.
detail: Ragang rises to 2,815 metres in the south of Lanao del Sur and has a base about 32 kilometres across. It is part of the Central Mindanao Arc of volcanoes, and Wikipedia calls it the most active volcano on Mindanao.
The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology lists 8 eruptions, the last in July 1916; some eruptions credited to nearby Makaturing may have been Ragang's.
Its long profile is known locally as the Sleeping Lady, and it is the view from the campsite on Mount Matampor across Lake Lanao.

before_you_go: It is an active volcano: check the PHIVOLCS bulletin before going.
Arrange visits outside Marawi through the provincial tourism office and go with local companions.
items.getting_there: Go from Marawi to Butig. A 2023 party led by the MSU Mountaineering Club made a courtesy call at the MILF satellite office in Barangay Sandab, Butig, and started from the trailhead in the same barangay, reaching Hunters' Camp (about 1,300 metres) the same day.

do.title: Camp at Hunters' Camp
do.detail: The usual campsite is at about 1,300 metres; the summit is roughly 3 hours above it.

do.title: Cross the black-sand gullies
do.detail: The first day's trail passes through leech-infested forest to gullies of black volcanic sand.

do.title: See Lake Lanao and Lake Makaturing from the top
do.detail: The summit looks north over Lake Lanao, with Lake Makaturing, Mount Latukan and the Piapayungan Range around it.

images.author: Nayef Lao
images.caption: Mount Makaturing seen from Macadar, Lanao del Sur

items.name: Mount Makaturing
items.summary: An active stratovolcano of 1,940 metres in Butig, whose old eruptions are tied to the history of the Maguindanao Sultanate.
detail: Makaturing stands 1,940 metres high in Butig, with a base about 29 kilometres across, and is one of the active volcanoes of the Central Mindanao Arc.

A travel writer on Cotabato history links an 18th-century eruption of Makaturing to the decline of the Maguindanao Sultanate. On 18 May 1947 a Philippine Air Force C-47 named Lili Marlene crashed on the mountain, killing General Edwin Andrews and 16 others, among them Senator Francisco Zulueta.
Bangsamoro officials visited Mount Makaturing from Barira in Maguindanao del Norte in 2022, while a road linking Barira to Butig was under construction.

eat.title: Labas on the way to Butig
eat.detail: A 2023 party bought labas, smoked bariles tuna, on the way to Butig and had it for dinner the night before the climb.

before_you_go: The climb takes 2 to 3 hours for experienced hikers.
Arrange visits outside Marawi through the provincial tourism office and go with local companions.
items.getting_there: The trail is in Barangay Bualan, Balindong, on the Gurain Range; experienced hikers take 2 to 3 hours to the campsite.

do.title: Camp on the summit
do.detail: The campsite looks over Lake Lanao to Mount Ragang and the Bukidnon ranges.

do.title: Pick out the Bukidnon peaks
do.detail: From the campsite you can see Mount Kitanglad and Mount Kalatungan in Bukidnon as well as Lake Lanao and Mount Ragang.

items.name: Mount Matampor
items.summary: A peak of the Gurain Range in Balindong with a campsite over Lake Lanao and Mount Ragang.
detail: Mount Matampor is in the Gurain Range at Barangay Bualan, Balindong. A photo from its campsite won the Lanao del Sur prize in the 2021 regional photo contest of the Ministry of Trade, Investments and Tourism.
From the campsite the view takes in Lake Lanao, Mount Ragang, and the Kitanglad Range and Mount Kalatungan in Bukidnon.

before_you_go: Arrange visits outside Marawi through the provincial tourism office and go with local companions.
items.getting_there: On the Iligan-Marawi road.
items.name: Pantuwaraya Lake National Park
items.summary: A small lake and national park of 20 hectares in Saguiaran, on the Iligan-Marawi road.
detail: The park covers 20 hectares around Lake Pantao Raya in Barangay Pantao Raya, Saguiaran. It was declared a national park in 1965 under Republic Act No. 4190.

It lies in the Lake Lanao-Agus River watershed, which feeds the Agus hydroelectric plants. The Iligan-Marawi road that reaches it also passes Basak Lake, Laguna de Calaganan, Talao Lake and Agus Lake.

before_you_go: Dress modestly. Wikivoyage notes that Muslim women in Marawi are expected to cover their hair, while non-Muslims are not required to.
items.getting_there: Inside the Mindanao State University main campus in Marawi.

do.title: Pair it with the Aga Khan Museum
do.detail: The museum is on the same campus; a blogger found it closed on a Sunday visit.

do.title: Look at the green colour scheme and the metalwork
do.detail: The mosque, a gift of the King of Saudi Arabia to MSU, is noted for its green colouring, the metalwork pattern of its minaret, the painted petals on its dome and the name of Allah on its spires.

items.name: King Faisal Mosque
items.summary: The mosque on the Mindanao State University campus, a gift of the King of Saudi Arabia, in green with painted petals on its dome.
detail: The mosque was donated by the King of Saudi Arabia to Mindanao State University. It follows a green colour scheme, with metalwork on its minaret, painted petals on its dome and the name of Allah on top of its spires.
Visitors to the campus usually see it together with the Aga Khan Museum; a delegation from Aceh toured both in July 2025.

items.getting_there: Inside the Mindanao State University main campus in Marawi.
items.best_time: December to April are the least rainy months at Marawi (about 140 to 185 mm a month) and May to July the wettest (330 to 415 mm); it is cool all year, with highs of 24 to 26°C.

do.title: Play a round on the 9-hole course
do.detail: The course is laid out on the rolling grounds of Mindanao State University.

do.title: Look over Lake Lanao and the city
do.detail: A heritage blogger calls the course a great place to view Lake Lanao and Marawi.

images.author: Patrickroque01
images.caption: The Mindanao State University Golf Course, Marawi

items.name: MSU Golf Course
items.summary: A 9-hole course on the Mindanao State University campus that is also a viewpoint over Lake Lanao and Marawi.
detail: The course lies on the rolling grounds of Mindanao State University. A heritage blogger calls it a great place to view Lake Lanao and the city.
The Marawi Resort Hotel is nearby on the campus.

items.getting_there: In Marawi, on 30,697 square metres cut from the Camp Amai Pakpak reservation, between 2 national highways and next to Marawi City National High School.
items.name: Lanao People's Park
items.summary: A park in Marawi on the site of Fort Marawi, where Amai Pakpak held off the Spanish, now marked by the National Historical Commission.
detail: In 1992 President Corazon Aquino took 30,697 square metres out of the Camp Amai Pakpak military reservation, formerly Camp Keithley, and reserved it for the Lanao People's Park and Public Library.

Markers identify it with Fort Marawi, the kota of Amai Pakpak: in August 2024 the National Historical Commission installed 2 here, on the 1891 battle between Amai Pakpak and Governor-General Valeriano Weyler and on the defence of Marawi against Weyler and Ramón Blanco.
The Bangsamoro heritage commission plans further archaeological work at Kota Marawi, now Barangay Camp Amai Pakpak.

items.name: Kilometer Zero of Mindanao
items.summary: The marker in Marawi used as the reference point for distances on the roads of Mindanao.
detail: Just as Luzon measures its roads from Rizal Park in Manila, Mindanao uses a Kilometer Zero marker in Marawi as the reference point for all its provinces.
The provincial tourism office lists Kilometer Zero among the attractions of Marawi.

before_you_go: Raft only with an organised operator, with helmets and life jackets.
items.name: Maradugao River
items.summary: The river on Wao's border with Bukidnon, run as a whitewater rafting trip of about 3 hours.
detail: The Maradugao marks the border between Wao and Bukidnon. A 2023 Philippine Information Agency feature describes whitewater rafting on it, on a stretch of up to 11 kilometres through about 7 barangays, taking about 3 hours.
The provincial tourism office has also named whitewater rafting in Wao among Lanao del Sur's draws.

before_you_go: The site is on community land; visit with the municipality's permission.
items.name: Kota Kalawi
items.summary: A Maranao fort on Lake Lanao, the site of a 1903 clash with the US Army and of the first archaeological dig in BARMM.
detail: Kota Kalawi is a Maranao defensive fort in Bacolod-Kalawi, built in response to American incursions. The Bangsamoro heritage commission records the Battle of Kota Kalawi of April 1903 here; nearby Kota Bacolod Grande was where the Sultan of Bacolod fought Captain John J. Pershing's forces that month.

Archaeologists from the University of the Philippines and Mindanao State University excavated the site, the first such dig in Lanao del Sur and BARMM, and presented their findings in May 2026. They traced occupation back to the Neolithic and found little evidence of the heavy fighting described in American reports.

before_you_go: It is farmland; ask the municipality or barangay before walking in.
items.name: Padang Karbala
items.summary: The field in Bayang where the Sultan of Bayang and his followers made their last stand against American forces in May 1902.
detail: Padang Karbala, the site of Kota Pandapatan, is where the Sultan of Bayang and his followers fought American forces in May 1902. The Bangsamoro heritage commission validated it as a historical site in 2023.
The land is farmed today. Locals point to patches of cement they say belonged to Camp Vicars, the American camp.

items.name: José Abad Santos execution site
items.summary: The place in Malabang where Chief Justice José Abad Santos was executed in 1942 for refusing to take an oath to the Japanese.
detail: José Abad Santos was executed in Malabang on 7 May 1942 for refusing to take the oath of allegiance to the Japanese forces.
The National Historical Commission of the Philippines marked the site on 6 March 2025.

before_you_go: It is a grave and a place of remembrance: dress modestly and ask before taking photos.
Go only with the heritage commission's or the municipality's arrangement.
items.name: Hashim and Mimbantas burial site
items.summary: The graves at Camp Bushra Somiorang in Butig of the MILF's founding chairman and its military chief, protected by Bangsamoro law.
detail: Sheikh Salamat Hashim, founding chairman of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front, and Alim Abdul Aziz Mimbantas, its vice chair for military affairs, are buried at Camp Bushra Somiorang in Butig.
Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 60 recognises the site as a protected heritage and tourism site, managed by a board chaired by the Bangsamoro heritage commission.

before_you_go: Go with the municipality's or the local organisers' arrangement; escorts were provided in 2019.
items.getting_there: About 1 hour by road from Cotabato City.

do.title: Swim under the falls
do.detail: Visitors swim in the pools and stand under the falling water for a water massage.

do.title: Cool off in the Ambal River
do.detail: Swimming in the Ambal River nearby is free of charge.

items.name: Bubuludtua Falls
items.summary: A swimming waterfall in Barira, about an hour from Cotabato City, on land that was once part of an MILF camp.
detail: Part of the site used to be a camp of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front and has been turned into a summer spot with the help of several local groups. In 2019 GMA News reported a PHP 10 entrance fee, swimming in cool mountain water, and MILF members acting as security escorts for visitors.

The Ambal River nearby is free for swimming. The Bangsamoro tourism bureau named the development of Bubuludtua Falls among the region's potential tourism projects in 2023, and regional officials visited it in 2022.

before_you_go: Dress modestly and ask before taking photos inside.
items.name: Masjid Alqudra
items.summary: A mosque in Barangay Bulalo, Sultan Kudarat, picked for the Maguindanao prize in the region's 2021 tourism photo contest.
detail: The Ministry of Trade, Investments and Tourism chose a photo of Masjid Alqudra in Bulalo, Sultan Kudarat, as the first-prize entry for Maguindanao in its 2021 photo contest, Bangsamoro: Revealing its Hidden Treasure.
The ministry describes it as a place of learning and moral guidance for the Maguindanaon community as well as of prayer.

images.author: Provincial Government of Maguindanao del Sur
images.caption: The National Historical Commission marker for Salipada K. Pendatun at his tomb.

items.name: Tomb of Salipada K. Pendatun
items.summary: The grave of the World War II guerrilla leader and lawmaker after whom his town is named, marked by the National Historical Commission.
detail: Salipada K. Pendatun (1912 to 1985) set up the guerrilla movement in Cotabato during World War II and later represented Maguindanao in the Regular Batasang Pambansa from 1984 to 1985.
The National Historical Commission of the Philippines placed a marker at his tomb in 2012. A 2026 travel feature on Maguindanao del Sur names the tomb among the province's historical places.

before_you_go: Dress modestly and ask before photographing the prayer hall.
items.getting_there: On the highway through Guindulungan.
items.best_time: Eid, when the mosque is the main venue for the town's congregational prayers; otherwise visit outside prayer times.

do.title: Look at the hand-painted calligraphy
do.detail: In 2024 a group of hafidz painted the interior walls with Qur'anic surahs and Islamic sayings.

images.author: Comenei Ali / Bangsamoro Information Office
images.caption: The white, green-domed front of Masjidil Haron Rashid with calligraphy along its arches.

images.author: Comenei Ali / Bangsamoro Information Office
images.caption: The prayer hall of Masjidil Haron Rashid, its walls painted with Qur'anic calligraphy.

images.author: Provincial Government of Maguindanao del Sur
images.caption: Masjidil Haron Rashid from the highway, with its tall white minaret and green dome.

items.name: Masjidil Haron Rashid
items.summary: A highway mosque in Guindulungan, opened in 1995, that sheltered MILF fighters during the war and is now painted inside with Qur'anic calligraphy.
detail: The first call to prayer sounded here on 20 January 1995, in Barangay Tambunan II, then part of Talayan and now of Guindulungan. The mosque was built on the initiative of Maguindanao Vice Governor Datu Midpantao Antao Midtimbang Sr. by local volunteers, on land that had held a market and later military housing.
During the armed struggle it was a meeting place and supply point for MILF fighters. In 2024 a group of hafidz painted its interior walls by hand with Qur'anic surahs and Islamic sayings.
Today it stands along the highway as a landmark of the town and hosts Eid prayers, iftar gatherings and Qur'an reading contests.

before_you_go: Visit with the municipality's or the heritage commission's arrangement.

images.author: Morsid Kadir / Bangsamoro Information Office
images.caption: A faded sign reading Residence of Salamat Hashim on the ruined house at Camp Abubakar.

items.name: Salamat Hashim residence, Camp Abubakar
items.summary: The 1990 house in the former MILF stronghold of Camp Abubakar where the movement's founder lived, the first site marked by the Bangsamoro heritage commission.
detail: Camp Abubakar was once a stronghold of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front. The residence of its founder, Sheikh Salamat Hashim, built in 1990, served as a command centre during the armed struggle.

On 3 July 2025 the Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage unveiled its first historical marker here. Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 61 provides for a memorial marker bearing the names of the fallen and an eco-park in the camp, still to be built.

items.getting_there: In Barangay Kalanganan, the same barangay as the Grand Mosque.
items.best_time: December, when Mother Kalanganan holds the Layagan crab festival.

do.title: Take in the view from the bridge
do.detail: The bridge on Timako Hill looks over Kalanganan II to the Grand Mosque.

items.name: Timako Hill
items.summary: A wooded coastal hill in Kalanganan, one of only 2 high points in Cotabato City, with monkeys, mangroves and a view of the Grand Mosque.
detail: Timako Hill rises on the coast of Barangay Kalanganan, facing Illana Bay, and is home to monkeys and other wildlife. A MindaNews feature calls it one of only 2 elevated areas in the city where the trees are protected (from a search snippet).
Around it are fishponds known for mud crabs, and the Timaco Mangrove Swamp, where a 2022 study counted 15 mangrove species, 2 of them threatened, but far fewer trees than an earlier survey.
A bridge on the hill gives a wide view over Kalanganan with the Grand Mosque behind. A new seaport was being built at its foot in 2018.

items.summary: The regional museum in the Bangsamoro Government Center, run by the Bangsamoro heritage commission since 2019.
detail: The Bangsamoro Museum opened in 2019 at the Bangsamoro Government Center, in the Shariff Kabunsuan Cultural Complex. It is run by the Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage and holds artefacts, artworks, oral histories and digitised records of the region.
It also hosts temporary exhibitions and workshops, such as the Landung art exhibit in February 2025 and a Teduray sayaf basket-weaving workshop on its 7th anniversary in February 2026.

items.name: Cojangan
items.summary: A calm, lagoon-like stretch of sea among the islets of Hadji Muhtamad, west of Basilan Island.
detail: Hadji Muhtamad is a young municipality made up of the Pilas Islands and other islets west of Basilan Island. Cojangan, in Barangay Palahangan, takes its name from the Sinama word lowang, a hole: it has a hole in the middle that looks like a lagoon. The ministry praises the freshness of its sea water and the calm.
A photo of Cojangan took the Basilan first prize in the 2021 regional photo contest of the Ministry of Trade, Investments and Tourism.

before_you_go: Arrange a visit through the provincial tourism office, which has given visitors free guides for the cost of fuel.

items.name: Maluso River
items.summary: The river of Maluso on south-western Basilan, noted as a source of fresh water for sailors in an 1843 sailing directory.
detail: Maluso lies on the south-western side of Basilan and is known for its beaches, rivers and wide mangroves. Its river, locally called Subah Maluso, is tied to the town's beginnings and was noted as a source of fresh water by European sailors; it appears in James Horsburgh's India Directory of 1843.
In July 2022 the town launched Marayaw Maluso, a programme to make it a peace and eco-tourism hub. A list of the region's waterfalls places Garlayan Falls and Mahayahay Falls in Maluso.

items.name: Kilantan Spring
items.summary: A cool spring in Ampatuan, on ground the Teduray hold as a sacred hunting ground.
detail: Kilantan Spring is one of the tourism sites the Maguindanao del Sur provincial government lists for the town of Ampatuan. The name comes from klan-taen, a word meaning chaos, drought, the dry season or the absence of water.

The province describes the place as a sacred hunting ground of the Teduray, the native inhabitants of the area. A 2026 Manila Times column on the province's lesser-known places notes the spring's cool water and the greenery around it.
before_you_go: The spring sits on ground the Teduray consider sacred; ask community leaders before visiting and follow their guidance.
No source gives directions, fees or opening hours; arrange the visit through the Ampatuan municipal hall or the provincial tourism office.

items.name: Bual Spring
items.summary: A spring of clear, cold pools in Sitio Bisang, kept by the Indigenous community around it.
detail: Bual Spring is in Sitio Bisang, Barangay Talisawa, Datu Abdullah Sangki. The provincial government says the spring, locally called bual, is maintained by the Indigenous community living around it and has long been the source of drinking water for the residents of Sitio Bisang.

Its cold, clear water draws small groups from nearby villages, mostly on weekends. The site is now promoted as Seven Pools, an eco-tourism spot, and the province says development there is meant to make room for visitors without spoiling the natural pools. A 2026 Manila Times column describes its naturally formed pools of clear freshwater.
before_you_go: The spring is still the drinking-water source of Sitio Bisang; do not use soap or shampoo and carry your rubbish out.
The site is looked after by the local Indigenous community; ask permission on arrival.
items.best_time: Weekends are when local visitors come, so go on a weekday for a quieter visit.

do.title: Swim in the natural pools
do.detail: The spring forms a series of naturally formed pools of cold, clear water.

items.name: Sa-Wa River
items.summary: A clear river pool about 7 feet deep in Sitio Tangkapa, Datu Hoffer Ampatuan.
detail: The Sa-Wa River flows through Sitio Tangkapa in Barangay Talibadok, Datu Hoffer Ampatuan. Where it runs over natural ground it forms a small pool of more or less 7 feet deep, which the provincial government lists among the town's tourism sites for anyone wanting a dip in clear water.

The provincial tourism list groups Datu Hoffer under the heading Mini Switzerland of MDS. The town is also home to Teduray craft communities; in Barangay Limpongo, women weave rattan and bamboo goods for sale.
before_you_go: The pool is more or less 7 feet deep; weaker swimmers should stay at the edge.
Arrange a guide through the Datu Hoffer Ampatuan municipal hall; no source gives directions or fees.

items.name: Limpongo Teduray crafts
items.summary: A Teduray village in Datu Hoffer Ampatuan where women make and sell rattan and bamboo goods.
detail: In Barangay Limpongo, Datu Hoffer Ampatuan, the Teduray welcome visitors with a display of rattan and bamboo crafts. The women of the Limpongo Women and Youth Association keep up techniques handed down through generations, and the enterprise gives them both an income and a way of keeping their heritage going.

The Teduray live between Maguindanao del Norte and Maguindanao del Sur. Their name is explained as coming from tew, meaning people, and duray, a tiny bamboo hook that stands for their skill at fishing. The provincial government also lists the Monom handbag, woven from onomen, as a Datu Hoffer handicraft.
before_you_go: The Tourism Promotions Board has picked communities in the province for community-based tourism; arrange a visit through the provincial tourism office.
Ask before photographing people at work, and buy from the makers directly.

items.name: Tamburi Falls
items.summary: A waterfall over layered rock into a cold pool in South Upi.
detail: Tamburi Falls is one of 2 waterfalls the Maguindanao del Sur provincial government lists for South Upi, alongside Kuhan Falls. Its water drops over the edge of a steep mountain slope into a pool below, and the falls are known for an unusual layered rock formation.
The province says residents of South Upi come for the clean, cold water. South Upi is Teduray country, where the Monom weaving and craft tradition is practised.
before_you_go: Go with a local guide arranged in South Upi; no source gives a route or trail conditions.
Rocks around falls are slippery; take care at the pool edge.

items.name: Miracle Mosque
items.summary: A mosque in Mamasapano that the community dates to 1444, known for a mimbar said to have survived a flood.
detail: The Maguindanao del Sur provincial government lists the Miracle Mosque among the tourism sites of Mamasapano. The community believes the mosque has stood since the 14th century, and gives a date of 5 March 1444.

Its name comes from a story told in the town. In 1951 a heavy flash flood swept through the area, but the mimbar, the pulpit inside the mosque, was not carried away. 3 ustadz of the community, Hadji Abdulmanan Matangkoy, Hadji Pawa Mulidis and Hadji Akmad Manalasal, tell of several more wonders connected with the mimbar.
before_you_go: Dress modestly: cover shoulders and knees, and women should bring a headscarf. Remove shoes before entering the prayer hall and avoid prayer times, especially Friday midday prayer.
This is a working mosque; ask the caretaker or imam before entering or taking photographs.

items.name: Tomb of Datu Udtog Matalam and the Old Mosque
items.summary: The tomb of a former governor of the old Cotabato province, beside an old mosque in Pagalungan.
detail: The tomb of Datu Udtog Matalam Sr., the first elected governor of the old Cotabato province, stands beside an old mosque in Pagalungan. The provincial government describes the 2 structures, side by side, as illustrating the old history of Central Mindanao, and credits Matalam with building harmonious relations between Muslims and Christian settlers in the region.

Matalam is also remembered for the manifesto he issued on 1 May 1968, 2 months after the Jabidah massacre, declaring the Muslim Independence Movement, which sought an independent state of Mindanao, Sulu and Palawan. Pagalungan itself was the capital of the old Cotabato province from 1966 to 1973.

Other landmarks from his time are nearby. The old NAWASA water tank, built while he was governor and declared a historical landmark by the town, is now home to thousands of bats. The old provincial jail is used as an evacuation centre, and the red house of the old Rural Bank of Greater Cotabato has been kept as a heritage site.
before_you_go: Dress modestly: cover shoulders and knees, and women should bring a headscarf. Remove shoes before entering the prayer hall and avoid prayer times, especially Friday midday prayer.
Ask the family or the caretaker before entering the tomb area.

items.name: Ampatuan massacre memorial
items.summary: The site in Sitio Masalay where 58 people, many of them journalists, were killed on 23 November 2009.
detail: On the morning of 23 November 2009, 58 people on their way to file a certificate of candidacy for governor for Esmael Mangudadatu, then vice-mayor of Buluan, were stopped in Ampatuan, kidnapped and killed at Sitio Masalay, Barangay Salman. The dead included Mangudadatu's wife and 2 sisters, lawyers, aides, passing motorists and journalists; Davao Today counts 32 journalists and Wikipedia at least 34. The Committee to Protect Journalists called it the single deadliest event for journalists since it began keeping records in 1992.

A memorial marker stands at the site with tombstones bearing the victims' names; Davao Today counted at least 38 tombstones in 2017. A separate monument was built nearby in remembrance of the victims.
Each year around 23 November, families and colleagues of the victims come to the site for a mass, light candles and lay flowers where the bodies were found.
before_you_go: This is a grave site; behave as you would at a cemetery and do not walk on the tombs.
Journalists visiting for the anniversaries have been escorted by the military and police; do not go on your own, and coordinate with local authorities first.
items.best_time: Families and media groups gather at the site for the anniversary around 23 November.

do.title: Join the anniversary commemoration
do.detail: Families and colleagues hold a mass at the site around 23 November and light candles at the memorial.

items.name: Old Maguindanao Provincial Capitol
items.summary: The P218-million capitol the Ampatuans built in Shariff Aguak, about 400 m from their mansions.
detail: Shariff Aguak was the first capital of Maguindanao, but the capitol moved to Sultan Kudarat after the 1986 People Power Revolution. Andal Ampatuan Sr., elected governor in 2001, brought the offices back to Shariff Aguak and then built a larger, 3-storey capitol, occupied before the 2007 election and inaugurated in March 2009 in the presence of President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo. It cost P218 million, P50 million of it from her social funds, and stands about 400 m from the mansions of the Ampatuan clan; the governor's wing even has a jacuzzi.

After the Maguindanao massacre of November 2009 the building was used as a warehouse. Governor Esmael Mangudadatu, elected in 2010, governed from his hometown of Buluan instead; his successor Mariam Mangudadatu moved back in 2019, and in July 2020 it served as a COVID-19 isolation facility. When Maguindanao was split in 2022, Buluan became the capital of Maguindanao del Sur.
A photograph released by the Philippine Army's 601st Infantry Brigade describes the old capitol as now housing one of the army's infantry brigades.
before_you_go: The building is described as an army brigade headquarters; ask permission before approaching or photographing it.

items.name: Mado Hot Spring National Park
items.summary: A 48-hectare national park around a hot spring near Awang Airport, set aside in 1939.
detail: Mado Hot Spring National Park is a protected area in Barangay Awang, Datu Odin Sinsuat, near Awang Airport. It covers 48 hectares around a medicinal hot spring, with a natural swimming pool and a health resort, and is governed by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources.

President Manuel L. Quezon declared it a national park on 25 September 1939 by Proclamation No. 456, reserving the land, then in the municipal district of Awang in the old Cotabato province, 'for the benefit and enjoyment of the people of the Philippines'. The proclamation placed it under the Bureau of Forestry and marked its corners with trees such as balobo, white lauan and apitong.
before_you_go: No current source describes the state of the pool or resort; ask in Datu Odin Sinsuat before making the trip.

items.name: Masjid Al-Nasser Abpi
items.summary: A white-and-gold mosque in Datu Odin Sinsuat, built in 2016, that holds more than 10,000 worshippers.
detail: Masjid Al-Nasser Abpi, known as the White Mosque, was built in 2016 by the Abpi family, whose roots are in Datu Piang, Maguindanao del Sur. It stands on a 20,000-square-metre property and can hold more than 10,000 worshippers. The idea came out of a conversation among the Abpi siblings, and the mosque is named after one of them, Al-Nasser Abpi; it began as a small mosque and was later enlarged.

The design is minimalist, white and gold inside and out, and the caretaker says it was inspired by the mosque in Madinah. Mashrabiya and glass windows let in air while keeping out the sun. There are small rooms for worshippers staying overnight for i'tikaf, and the mosque is lent free of charge for markaz graduations and nikah weddings.
A travel writer who toured the province with its tourism office notes that the mosque stands out especially against the dusk sky.
before_you_go: Dress modestly: cover shoulders and knees, and women should bring a headscarf. Remove shoes before entering the prayer hall and avoid prayer times, especially Friday midday prayer.
Parking is at the back of the mosque; it fills up on Eid'l Fitr and Eid'l Adha.

items.name: Ranao Pilayan Falls
items.summary: A modest waterfall in the Upi uplands, 10 minutes' walk from the trailhead.
detail: Ranao Pilayan Falls is one of several waterfalls on the slopes of Upi, which PhilAtlas lists with Kiga, Sapala and Tabuan Falls in the same municipality. Ranao Pilayan is also the name of a barangay of Upi.

A network of gentle trails leads to the falls, which a travel writer touring the province with its tourism office described as modest but striking. The cascade is a brisk 10-minute walk from the trailhead.

items.name: Forever Tulip Garden
items.summary: A garden in Lamitan of 30,000 tulips cut from recycled plastic bottles.
detail: The city government of Lamitan opened the Forever Tulip Garden on 23 September 2019 at Sitio Panansangan, Barangay Ubit. Its 30,000 tulips were cut from 26,877 plastic bottles gathered from 45 villages of the city and painted red, yellow, pink and blue; other bottles were mixed into sand and cement to make the garden paths.

The garden came out of the city's solid waste campaign under then mayor Rose Furigay, Abante Lamitan, Atras Basura, and visitors were already coming before it was finished. In 2025 the Daily Tribune still listed it among Basilan's attractions, alongside Bulingan Falls.
before_you_go: Coordinate with the Lamitan City tourism office before visiting places outside the city centre; it arranges guides and transport.

items.name: Ambalang Museum and GAMABA Weaving Center
items.summary: A weaving school and museum in Lamitan honouring the Yakan master weaver Apuh Ambalang Ausalin.
detail: Ambalang Ausalin (1943–2022) was a Yakan master weaver from Lamitan, known for sinalu'an and seputangan, 2 of the most intricate Yakan textiles. She learned from her mother, reputed to be the best weaver in Basilan, and received the National Living Treasures Award (Gawad sa Manlilikha ng Bayan) in 2016. She died at her home in Parangbasak, Lamitan, in February 2022.

The GAMABA Weaving Center in Lamitan also works as a School of Living Tradition, where she taught a new generation of magtetenum (weavers) to make tennun, Yakan for woven cloth. In June 2024 her eldest son, Berty Ausalin, led the inauguration of the weaving centre and the Ambalang Museum on Yakan culture.

Yakan cloth is woven in geometric patterns in bright, contrasting colours. A 2-metre cloth takes between 2 weeks and a month to make, and designs include the rainbow-like palipattang, the python-inspired buga-sama and the vine-patterned dawen-dawen.
before_you_go: Hand-woven tennun takes weeks to make; pay the asking price rather than haggling.
Ask before photographing weavers at their looms.

items.name: Kumalarang River
items.summary: Basilan's westward-flowing river, with waterfalls and a stone said to mark a French landing of the 1840s.
detail: The Kumalarang River flows west through the western half of Basilan and is also called Baunuh Peggesan; Kumalarang was also one of the old names given to the whole island. Chinese texts of the Ming dynasty mention a Kingdom of Kumalarang, believed to have been on the island's north-western shore. The Basilan provincial article on Wikipedia lists the waterfalls of the Kumalarang River among the island's natural attractions.

French archives show that the French navy spent 6 months surveying Basilan in 1844 and 1845, and that France tried and failed to acquire the island. The archives say the French etched a landmark into stone on the banks of the Kumalarang River in Lantawan, and in 2026 the Bangsamoro heritage commission in Basilan led a mission to find the landing site.
before_you_go: The river runs through Lantawan and Isabela City; Isabela is not part of BARMM, so check which side you are visiting.
Go with guides arranged through the Basilan provincial tourism office.

items.name: Punta Matangal
items.summary: A peninsula point in Tuburan that Basilan's travel guides name as a surf spot.
detail: Punta Matangal is a peninsula point in Tuburan, on Basilan. The Wikivoyage guide to the province describes it as a haven for surfers, comparing it with the north shores of Hawaii.

Matangal is an old name: in Yakan oral tradition it was one of the names of prehistoric Basilan, taken from a mountain farther east that, like Basilan Peak, served Maguindanao traders as a landmark when sailing the Celebes Sea.
before_you_go: No source gives current surf conditions, access or facilities; ask the Basilan provincial tourism office before going.
Travel writers strongly advise against going far from Basilan's town centres without a local guide.

items.name: Saluag Island
items.summary: The southernmost island of the Philippines, a 1.6 km strip of white sand with 2 lighthouses.
detail: Saluag Island, part of the municipality of Sibutu, is the southernmost island of the Philippines and is 1.6 km long. Locally it is called Sikulan.

A small community of Sama Dilaut and Tausug live there, off waters rich in fish and seaweed. The island has fine white sand, green bush and 2 lighthouses, one old and rusted and the other a modern working light.
before_you_go: Register with the tourism office in Bongao before visiting the outer islands, and follow the advice of local authorities.
People live on the island; ask before photographing homes and residents.
items.getting_there: From Tandu Banak or Sibutu proper, take a habal-habal (motorcycle taxi) to Tandu Owak, then charter a boat; the crossing takes about 30 minutes.

items.name: Sanga-Sanga Island
items.summary: The island between Bongao and Tawi-Tawi that holds the province's airport and its boatyards.
detail: Sanga-Sanga lies between Tawi-Tawi Island to the east and Bongao Island to the south, and its 11 barangays all belong to Bongao. Sanga-Sanga Airport, the main airport of the province, is on the island, about 15 minutes from Bongao town.
During the Second World War the island was a major stopover of the Japanese navy; American forces liberated it on 2 April 1945 and it was then used by American and Australian forces.

Walking around Sanga-Sanga you pass large wooden boats being built by local craftsmen, most of them Sama-Bajau. One builder told a SunStar writer that a wooden prahu takes about a year to build, all by hand.
before_you_go: Ask before photographing boatbuilders and their yards.
items.getting_there: The island is joined to Bongao by road; tricycles and habal-habal run between the airport and Bongao town in about 15 minutes.

items.name: Tawi-Tawi Island
items.municipality: Languyan, Panglima Sugala, Tandubas and Bongao
items.summary: The main island of the province: hilly, wooded and home to birds found nowhere else.
detail: Tawi-Tawi Island is the main island of the province, with a little more than half its land. At 580.5 km² it is the 21st-largest island of the Philippines and the third-largest in the Sulu Archipelago, about 55 km long and between 10 and 23 km wide, rising to 549 m. It is of volcanic origin, hilly and heavily wooded, with white sand beaches and rocky coasts, and is shared by Bongao, Languyan, Panglima Sugala and Tandubas.

The island supports many endemic species, among them the Tawitawi brown dove and the Sulu hornbill, while the Sulu bleeding-heart may already be extinct. Clearing for farms and settlements in recent decades has sharply reduced their forest, and many of these birds are listed as critically endangered.
before_you_go: Register with the tourism office in Bongao before travelling beyond the town, and travel with a local guide.
items.getting_there: From Bongao, a jeepney leaves daily from the public market for Panglima Sugala and Languyan.

items.name: Pahut
items.summary: A dive site in Bongao where a Second World War plane wreck lies among the corals.
detail: Pahut, in Bongao, is one of the dive sites around the provincial capital. Divers see corals and fish, and the wreck of a Second World War plane, which a Lakwatsero guide identifies as an old Japanese war plane.
There is a beach resort in Pahut, and the Tawi-Tawi Divers Club is the contact the guide gives for scuba diving around Bongao.
before_you_go: Dive only with a local dive operator; no source gives depth or current conditions at the wreck.
Leave the wreck as you find it.

items.name: Bajau village of Bongao
items.summary: A Sama Dilaut community of stilt houses and footbridges in Bongao, known for its woven mats.
detail: In Bongao, a Sama Dilaut (Bajau) community lives in stilt houses joined by wooden footbridges that run out over the sea. Visitors come to see a day in their sea-based life.
The village is known for weaving, especially the colourful banig, hand-woven mats that many of the women make every day, and travel guides send visitors here to buy souvenirs.
before_you_go: This is a living neighbourhood; go with a local guide and ask before photographing people or their homes.
Footbridges can be narrow and uneven.

items.name: Takumi Butai Memorial Shrine
items.summary: A memorial to a Japanese wartime commander and the Japanese soldiers who died in Cotabato City.
detail: The Takumi Butai Memorial Shrine honours Takumi, the provincial commander of the Japanese forces in Cotabato City during the Second World War, and the Japanese soldiers who died in the city. Before he died Takumi asked that some of his ashes be buried in Cotabato City.
The shrine was built by the Lions Club of Kyoto, Japan, together with the city government. Wikivoyage lists it among the city's sights.
before_you_go: Treat the shrine as a grave and a war memorial.

items.name: Immaculate Conception Cathedral
also_known_as: Metropolitan Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
items.summary: The seat of the Archdiocese of Cotabato, on Quezon Avenue.
detail: The Metropolitan Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception is the seat of the Archdiocese of Cotabato, which covers Cotabato City, Maguindanao del Norte, Maguindanao del Sur, western Cotabato and most of Sultan Kudarat. GCatholic dates the cathedral parish to 1954, and the Church named it one of its jubilee churches for the 500 years of Christianity in the Philippines and for the Holy Year 2025.

The diocese grew from the Territorial Prelature of Cotabato and Sulu, created in 1950, and was raised to a metropolitan archdiocese by Pope John Paul II on 5 November 1979. Its patron feast is the Immaculate Conception on 8 December. It is a different church from the older Immaculate Conception church at Tamontaka.
before_you_go: Dress modestly and keep quiet during Mass.
items.getting_there: On Quezon Avenue, Cotabato City.
items.best_time: The patron feast of the Immaculate Conception on 8 December.

items.name: Camp Keithley
items.summary: The site of an American army post of 1903 in Marawi, now being excavated by archaeologists.
detail: After the Battle of Bayang in May 1902 and Pershing's campaigns around Lake Lanao, American forces set up a post called Camp Marahui at the foot of Signal Hill in 1903. Later that year Meranaw warriors attacked the camp, killing several American soldiers, among them Private Fernando Guy Keithley. In 1905 it was renamed Camp Keithley, the first military camp named after a private. A monument put up in 1939 was removed during the Japanese occupation in 1942.

The Camp Keithley Archaeological Project of the University of the Philippines School of Archaeology, with the Bangsamoro heritage commission and the tourism ministry, dug 4 trenches in Barangay Datu Saber, looking for old settlements, kota (forts), colonial military structures and conflict sites. Finds shown in Marawi in June 2026 included earthenware, obsidian and chert, glass and metal objects; the project hopes they will also shed light on Meranaw life before Islam.
before_you_go: The excavation is a research site; see the finds through exhibits rather than entering the trenches.
items.getting_there: In Barangay Datu Saber, Marawi City, at the foot of Signal Hill.

items.name: Salikata National Park
items.summary: A forested national park of waterfalls, cliffs and a river gorge in the foothills of Mount Ragang.
detail: Salikata National Park lies in Lumba-Bayabao, in the thickly forested foothills of the Mount Ragang (Piapayungan) range. It is one of the 6 national parks of Lanao del Sur declared in 1965.
The park takes in waterfalls, a river gorge, rocky cliffs and dense forest canopy along the valley of the Gata River, from Barangay Salaman to Mapantao near the provincial border with Cotabato.
before_you_go: No source describes trails or visitor facilities; ask in Lumba-Bayabao for a local guide.

items.name: Rungkunan National Park
items.summary: A mountain forest park east of Marawi in the Lake Lanao and Agus River watershed.
detail: Rungkunan National Park covers the mountainous eastern part of Lanao del Sur in Ditsaan-Ramain and Tagoloan II, about 10 km east-south-east of Marawi. It lies near the Lake Lanao and Agus River watershed and is known for its sparkling stream, virgin forest and invigorating climate.
It was declared a national park in 1965 by Republic Act No. 4190.
before_you_go: No source describes trails or visitor facilities; ask locally for a guide.

items.name: Agus River
items.summary: The fast river that drains Lake Lanao through Marawi to Iligan Bay and powers much of Mindanao.
detail: The Agus River flows out of Lake Lanao from a narrow depression on its north-western rim and runs through Marawi to Iligan Bay, splitting near the sea into the channels that feed Maria Cristina Falls and Tinago Falls. Its current reaches up to 30 miles an hour in places, so it cannot be navigated along its whole length.

The hydroelectric plants on the river generate 70% of Mindanao's electricity, but the dams that regulate them have changed the levels of Lake Lanao and caused conflict with the people around it. In Maranao tradition, the Archangel Gabriel made the river to drain the lake when its rising waters threatened to drown the people of Sebangan. Wikivoyage notes that it flows between Saduc and Lilod in Marawi.
before_you_go: Do not swim in the fast-flowing stretches.

notes:
44 places: the 21 from places.ts (summary, detail and before_you_go copied verbatim; kind, sources, images, getting_there and best_time added) and 23 new ones. Sulu is excluded throughout.

Security: the UK FCDO advice (gov.uk, updated 15 July 2026) advises against all travel to western and central Mindanao and the Sulu archipelago, which covers all of BARMM. Every new entry carries that line in before_you_go. The 21 guide entries keep places.ts's before_you_go unchanged, so they do not carry it; the site may want to add it. The US State Department advisory page refused plain fetches (HTTP 403) and is not used.

Doubts in places.ts worth checking: it calls the Cotabato Grand Mosque the largest in the Philippines, but Wikipedia now gives that title to the rebuilt Marawi Grand Mosque (20,000 capacity against 15,000). It puts Kawayan Torogan in Marantao; the 2018 PRECUP registry puts it in Pompongan-a-Marantao, a barangay of Marawi City, and the matter is unsettled. It calls Bud Bongao 314 m; Wikipedia gives 317 m for the view deck on Tambisan Peak. It dates Tamontaka Church to the 1870s; Wikipedia says 1872, moved to its present site in 1879, and rebuilt after the 1976 earthquake.

Municipality notes: Malamawi Island is in Isabela City (Region IX), as places.ts itself says. Basilan National Park is listed under Lamitan, but the park spans Isabela City, Lamitan, Tipo-Tipo and Sumisip. Fort Pikit is listed under Malidegao (SGA, created 2024).
